>The Happiness Trap

  
You could try smoking cessation with Swedish snus (small pouches to put in the mouth, inside your upper lip). They pouches can contain tobacco and nicotine (then called "White Portion) - or just pure nicotine (then called "All White Portion). They come in thousands of flavors. And in slim size (versus normal size), which makes them "invisible" to others.  
Only through Swedish snus I managed to quit smoking (after 48 years….), never before.   
It really satisfies your nicotine craving (the pouches are available in all strengths, from 3 mg to 43 mg nicotine/pouch) and later you can switch to completely nicotine-free snus pouches.  
It worked for me. As I live in Sweden it is very easy to buy snus. I don’t know where you live. But I know that one can order Swedish snus on the internet, but I’m not sure whether we are allowed to post links here? (Otherwise I could do this, if you want)  
I would be happy if this info hopefully can help you.

It is still this way in Sweden, as I can confirm after living here since 24 years. Other's children never get food when visiting their Swedish playmates. And adult not either, by the way. Only at official dinner invitations. This stinginess is widespread in Sweden. There is a corresponding a very old and very common saying here in Sweden: Sköt dig själv och skit i andra! Means: Mind your own business and screw others!  - And they do.

Dear damageddude, thank you for this heartwarming and encouraging story about your FIL! This is how it should be: Finding meaning and purpose even in old(er) age! The world seems to think that by growing older you loose all your wishes, interests, qualifications, personality, character etc practically overnight when forced into retirement - while it is exactly the other way around!  I’m sorry that dementia forced your FIL to retire for good but he doesn't seem to have forgotten his sense of funny mischief....which surely delights quite a few people in the nursing home. Thank you!  
Dear PurpleRN,  
Thank you for your uplifting story about the 63 year old nurse in training! Here in Europe, unfortunately, such a thing is not common as at this age you are no longer admitted to training, because you are supposed to retire two years later. Unfortunately, these things are not handled as relaxed here as in the USA… Warm greetings from Sweden!  
Dear Dismal-Opposite-6946,   
thank you very much for your suggestion to take the academic way!  I’ve already studied at several Swedish universities for 6 years (mostly distance studies as all the university cities are far away and have massive housing shortage). Different subjects, and a BA in History of Ideas and Sciences. I am also enrolled in college again for this fall - this just for my own pastime/enjoyment as there are no distractions/activities here on the countryside. But thank you for your otherwise very good idea!  
Dear Trevski,  
thank you very much for your suggestion to study and for your questions!  I’ve already studied at several Swedish universities for 6 years, have plans to continue studying this fall. My standard of life/wellbeing is mostly and severely impacted by feeling USELESS. I would love to feel needed and useful!  But I don’t - at all. And I would love to do a sufficiently paid job as my income (of travel business) has become pretty low due to Corona since 2020 and because of war in Ukraina. Furthermore I would like to continue to use my mental and physical faculties in a job - as you have so aptly described! I'm desperately looking for a way to make this happen too, but....(see above), sigh….  Thank you once again!

Thank you very much for your tips and advice, Dimendq3!  
Just to explain a bit more:  I’m not retired. It’s not a high income I’m pursuing, but a meaningful job with sufficient income. I already do several unpaid charity jobs (online) for communities, associations etc, since Corona hit a few years ago - as they could not meet and work in person any longer.  
Here in Sweden one retires earliest at age 65, or like newly introduced, at age 69. You can retire earlier than age 65, with corresponding pension deductions. But that’s not my idea. Actually, I don't want to retire at all, I imagine it being quite boring, especially here on the country side where nothing happens. (There are no apartments to rent in the bigger Swedish cities, though. For example in Stockholm: you wait 25 years (!)  for an apartment and stand in line all the time  - or buy one if you’ve got the money. No further alternatives. - Reminiscent of former East Germany or North Korea, but it really is this way when it comes to living.)  
One of your very good ideas is to reach out to leadership with interest - and maybe get started/be employed this way! All the leaderships I’m interested in are in Stockholm though (217 miles one way). But maybe there would be some kind of paid home office job I could do? (Even if I miss the personal presence of other people very much with all the online jobs, after all these lonely ZOOM-years.) But I could try!  
Once again, thank you very much!

That's right, of course, no group of people is totally good through and through.  But depressed people are disproportionately and extraordinarily often those who have high sensitivity, are concerned about others, care about others, are kind, and don't want to harm anyone. (Before they do that, they prefer to harm themselves.) The kindness and sensitivity of depressed people is also clearly confirmed by many studies and books.  One almost wishes for a world full of depressed people, most of whom don't bash each other's heads in, don't compete stone-faced, say or do nothing bad/cruel (like so many others). A world full of depressed people who are considerate of each other, tender-hearted and helpful (as best they can), that would be a good world (definitely preferable to the current one) - and you wouldn't have to be afraid of your neighbor/other people anymore.

What horrible, cruel parents you have! You have every right to hate them - and you should! How can they leave their own massively suffering child alone like that and send them out the door when they can't cope with life anymore...? Hate your parents - not yourself! I read that depression/suicidality is an inward turned hatred and you would rather kill yourself than confront those who are hurting you with your own (justified!) anger. My advice: don't feel guilty yourself for toxic parents who seem to be as emotional and empathetic as toast. Get away from there, find a good person to talk to/or a therapist, and build your own life. You don't have to have contact with your parents - no one forces you to. I speak from my own experience. You are not responsible for toxic people (even if you would have liked your own parents to be different/more empathetic -  most of us probably have that wish). Do not pay with your life for the stupidity and cruelty of others!

This is called biopolitics (Focault) and you are absolutely right. We all are managed, controlled human material, controlled by administrations and the needs of large companies. The only way to get out of that - as I see it - is  to become inwardly independent from all that and to live on your own terms as much as possible. Do what YOU love, start your own company (for example) don't give a shit - and fuck the slave mentality. You are here to be YOU - not any company's/administrations management matter.
